semantics: Refactor candidates that were investigated, costed and refused, as data rather than prose, so that nobody re-proposes them. The format is section 2 of .agents/docs/implemented/process/2026-09-20-agent-refactorability-gates.md; the ratchet suite that note describes has been removed, and nothing replaces it. Each candidate carries an `id`, the `candidate` refused, `why` it was refused, a `ruling` anchor holding the evidence, and the `symbols` whose shape the refusal reasons about. Each symbol's `signature` records the declaration as it stood when the entry was last checked against the code (bodies elided as `{…}`, comments stripped, whitespace collapsed); every entry was re-read against main on 2026-11-19. An optional `reopenWhen` states, in one sentence, the condition under which the refusal no longer holds and the candidate may be proposed again; an entry without one is refused on its reasons alone. An entry refuses a change: one that only records that an audit misread the code does not belong here. No test checks the file: a symbol whose shape has since changed is a cue to re-read the ruling, and the PR that changes the shape or removes a reason updates the entry, deleting it when no reason remains. Citing the candidate's `id` in the PR body is a convention, not checked. Re-proposing a refused candidate as originally specified is the failure this exists to stop; landing a candidate on NEW evidence is legal, and that PR cites the id, states what changed, and deletes or rewrites the entry.

candidates.candidate: ModelRetryGate onto the effect/persistence CircuitBreaker, with Effect.retry on its rejections behind the unchanged withRoutes
candidates.why: The breaker cannot keep the gate's backoff rule. Its opening count survives a close and resets only by time, once the circuit has stayed closed as long as it was last open (node_modules/effect/src/persistence/CircuitBreaker.ts:15-16, :1047-1051, :1208-1209, effect 4.1.4); a success while closed clears only the trip streak (:1269), and the next opening counts from the count the failing call started under (:522). The gate ends its streak on the first clean round-trip of a healthy route and never on a probe success (`recordExit` in packages/harness/src/agent/runtime/ModelRetryGate.ts, from #9078 and kept by #14781), so a released herd that fails at once grows the backoff while a route failing between successes stays at the base. Measured with one clean success between each recovery and the next failure: the gate cooled 1000 ms seven times; the breaker (jittered exponential from 1 s, capped at 5 min, midpoint jitter) opened for 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 32000 and 64000 ms. Every 5xx, 408, 409 and 429 not scoped to the model cools the whole wire route (packages/llm/src/errors.ts:146-147, :189-193), so an intermittently overloaded provider would stall every run on that credential toward the 5-minute cap; a constant openDuration brings back the herd re-failing at the base backoff that #9078 fixed. The breaker also never waits (CircuitBreaker.ts:21-22, :1213-1228) and withRoutes cannot add an error, so it would poll for as long as the probe runs, a whole billed turn (`ModelInvoker.invoke`), where a cooling route's callers wait out the backoff, one goes through as the probe, and the rest go with it once the route opens (`through` in ModelRetryGate.ts). classify has seen whether the call is the probe since effect 4.1.1 ({ probe }), which answers none of the reasons above; the module is @stability experimental (:154). The gate's base backoff is now one constant (RETRY_BACKOFF_MS) rather than a per-call baseBackoffMs, so a per-breaker openDuration is no longer a reason.

candidates.why: effect 4.1.4's McpClient (@stability experimental) speaks one protocol revision per client and fails any other answer: its ProtocolVersion is 2025-11-25 | 2026-07-28 (node_modules/effect/src/ai/McpClient.ts:70, :839, :860), it sends initialize once (:381-387), and a server answering another revision fails with UnsupportedError (:402-407). candidates.candidate: GitHub subscriptions as an RcMap keyed by target, with a PubSub per entry each binding consumes through Stream.fromPubSub, and the poll fiber forked in the entry's scope
candidates.why: Three facts the design does not survive. (1) A processLayer may require only PluginLayerServices (packages/harness/src/tools/toolTable.ts), which lack Secrets and HttpClient, so an RcMap made there cannot type a lookup that starts the poll; RcMap merges the getter's context into the lookup at run time (node_modules/effect/dist/RcMap.js get), so it would work only behind a cast that hides the requirement. (2) The run bindings are needed anyway (list, unbind, unbindAll, the per-run annotation level), so the RcMap's reference count would be a second count of the same fact; a target that ends itself (a closed PR, a rejected token) then has to leave both, and RcMap.invalidate plus releases from another fiber leave a window where a new bind reuses the dying entry, whose FiberHandle still holds the finishing poller. (3) A PubSub subscriber takes events on its own fiber, so an event published but not yet taken is outside the FiberSet the shutdown drain awaits, and is lost at shutdown. What landed instead: one Map from target path to its runs, the poll fibers in one FiberMap keyed by the same path (the last unbind removes the key; a poller that ends removes its subscription in its own step), and deliveries forked into one FiberSet at publish time.

candidates.candidate: the desktop window as one FiberHandle: open as FiberHandle.run with onlyIfMissing, the closed event as FiberHandle.clear, the shutdown as awaitEmpty, the quit's resume as a Deferred

candidates.candidate: a child's end report supplied by its launch (a report builder the launch hands its run), so `childEndReport` has no switch on `config.script.kind`
candidates.why: A launch knows the kind, but a run is launched more than once: a resume (`resumeRun`, `resumeOwnedChild`) is the same `executeAgent` over the run's stored configuration, with no launcher's closure behind it, and a background script stopped by a person is resumed exactly that way. The only durable carrier of the kind is `config.script`, so a supplied builder would be chosen from `config.script.kind` again where the launch is built (`executeAgent`), and would add a `RunLaunch` field plus an option threaded through `startChildRun` and `ExecuteAgentOptions` to carry the answer: the same decision, in a new place, with two more elements. The two reports also share nothing to factor (a script's reads its calls from the view, a subagent's its output and program result). What landed instead (2026-11-19): the fallback for a report that cannot be built, which read the kind a second time in `endRun`, is inside `childEndReport`, so one function owns the decision. Found in PR 1's record (§3) and carried as lane 9's last open item.
